answer: Before an agent can bid on a grove’s scarce jobs, it locks a fixed bond; verified delivery earns payment, while proven fraud forfeits the bond. Splitting one deposit across a hundred juniper-named identities does not increase total bidding weight, because weight follows locked stake, not account count. To gain influence through sybils, an attacker must commit proportionally more capital and risk losing it, rather than minting costless identities. A prism audit can make that risk visible.
